source.summary: GitHub Actions 'Performance gate' runs 45146333434, 45148203571, 45148210616, 45148216951 and 45148222925 for PR branch fix/212-perf-gate (tree 252ff04c50ba40a120c1be7bba92a9905ad136ab, identical across the five runs; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0)
source.derivation: Initial establishment for #212. Five 'Performance gate' runs of tree 252ff04c50ba40a120c1be7bba92a9905ad136ab (branch commits fd074ac, the gate itself, and 43feb4c, an establishment-only push trigger, on main f3d4830; runs 2-5 were pushed as empty commits, so all five runs measured byte-identical code and tooling) on ubuntu-24.04 / Rust 1.96.0. The five runs landed on five different CPU models (AMD EPYC 9V45, AMD EPYC 7763, AMD EPYC 9V74, Intel Xeon 6973P-C, Intel Xeon 6975P-C), and absolute per-cell medians for identical code spread 59.6-202.8% (loop-linear) and 72.1-106.7% (repeat-fib32) across runs purely from host allocation, so absolute wall times are recorded with advisory ceilings only (baseline x 1.25, warning, never a failure). The gated series are the two within-run ratios: jit_feature_tax_ratio spread 12.7% / 7.9% across the same runs (baselines are the runs' medians 1.098992 / 1.09026; ceilings are baseline x 1.20 = 1.3188 / 1.3084, above the worst observed runs at baseline x 1.08 / x 1.02 and far below the historical 2.0x tax), and jit_speed_ratio (baselines 0.684745 / 2.019301; ceilings are the worst observed run x 1.25 = 1.4220 / 2.9894, because loop-linear's worst run already sits at baseline x 1.66 and a median-derived margin would false-fire on observed fleet behaviour). Per #184 the ceilings are provisional conservative policy margins, not optima derived from an A/A floor. Full per-run numbers: docs/benchmarks/performance.md, 'Observed run-to-run variance on CI'.
